title: Fohlio
problem: Years of growth left Fohlio with inconsistent interfaces and fragmented workflows. The redesign had to simplify daily work while preserving existing projects and familiar interactions.
overview: Fohlio helps architecture and construction teams manage specifications, sourcing, and materials. I modernized its workflows and introduced AI-assisted features.

sections.title: Challenge
blocks: Teams spent too much time navigating between tools. The redesign needed shared interface patterns, easier access to information, and compatibility with existing projects.

sections.title: My Role & Process
blocks: I moved from research to hypotheses, prototypes, and validation, then turned tested patterns into reusable components.

sections.title: Project Analytics
blocks: Teams needed a view of budgets, resources, and project health across concurrent projects.
I prioritized metrics with project managers and designed a dashboard with access to project details.
Project managers reported 40% faster decisions and more accurate budget forecasts.

sections.title: Workflow Unification
blocks: Moving between modules made common tasks harder to follow.
I introduced consistent navigation, contextual breadcrumbs, and shortcuts.
Early testing showed 35% fewer clicks for common tasks and higher satisfaction scores.

sections.title: Library Update
blocks: A cluttered library made materials hard to find and manage.
I reorganized categories, search, and filters, added bulk actions and smart collections, and placed product details in a split-view side sheet.
The target was to halve the time spent searching for materials; this was a goal, not a measured result.

sections.title: Search by Image
blocks: Teams had reference images but often lacked product names.
I designed an image-upload flow with feedback on match quality. Visual search and Google Lens integration connect photos and moodboards to library products.
The goal was to shorten sourcing time and improve specification accuracy.

sections.title: Similar Items
blocks: Unavailable or over-budget products left teams searching for alternatives.
I designed recommendations based on style, specifications, and price, with a comparison view for evaluating matches.
The goal was to help teams complete specifications and avoid procurement delays.

sections.title: Prototypes & Packages
blocks: Creating product packages for each project took time and invited errors.
I designed reusable templates with grouping, customization, early cost estimates, and exports.
The projected reduction in package creation time was 60%; this was not a measured result.

sections.title: Table Reskin
blocks: The platform’s most-used component suffered from cramped layouts and inconsistent behavior.
I revised table typography and spacing, with customizable columns, inline editing, sorting, and filtering.
At the time of the study, development was underway and early testers responded positively to readability and usability.

list: Navigation: shared breadcrumbs and quick actions.
Tables: consistent sorting, filtering, and inline editing.
Tokens: common colors, typography, spacing, and elevation.

sections.title: Outcomes & Learnings
blocks: Modernizing Fohlio taught me to introduce change without discarding what teams already know. Shared navigation and table patterns gave the redesign a foundation; each new workflow still needed testing on its own merits.

blocks.title: SpeCurate: designing a new platform
blocks.text: Follow the later work on approvals, spatial planning, and reusable standards.
